title: Transfer Learning: Freeze the Backbone, Train the Head

questions.question: What is frozen in the local transfer-learning fixture?
options: The deterministic backbone_features computation; only the linear head has update state
The labels, while every image pixel is optimized
The final logits after they are computed
Nothing; train_head updates a hidden convolutional checkpoint
questions.explanation: backbone_features is a fixed NumPy feature function. train_head allocates and updates only its weights and bias.

questions.question: What shape does backbone_features return for nine RGB images?
options: (9, 3), regardless of the image size
(9, 12), for three means, three standard deviations, and two three-channel edge summaries
(3, 9), because channels are the first axis
(9, H, W, 3), because feature extraction does no reduction
questions.explanation: The local extractor concatenates four groups with three values each, producing 12 features per image.

questions.question: For parameter_counts(100, 12, freeze_backbone=True), how many parameters are trainable?
questions.explanation: The backbone's 100 parameters are frozen, while the 12 head parameters remain trainable.

questions.question: With stages [stem, stage1, head], base_lr=1e-3, and decay=0.1, which stage receives the largest discriminative rate?
options: stem
stage1
All three are forced to zero
head
questions.explanation: The helper applies the fewest decay factors to the last stage, so head receives 1e-3 while earlier stages are smaller.

questions.question: What does a decreasing train_head history on the seeded fixture establish?
options: That the local fixed features allow the linear head to reduce its cross-entropy
That the features came from an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet
That the schedule is optimal for every downstream dataset
That the frozen backbone's weights changed during training
questions.explanation: The history is evidence about this local optimization problem only; it says nothing about provenance, universal schedules, or frozen feature mutation.

questions.question: Why must a transfer-learning handoff name the frozen layers and optimizer groups?
options: It allows the caller to skip all shape and label validation
A learning-rate value alone cannot tell which parameters can change
It proves a low learning rate prevents overfitting
It turns a local feature fixture into a downloaded checkpoint
questions.explanation: Ownership and optimizer membership determine the actual update boundary; the local parameter-count and rate reports make that boundary auditable.
